newsitem.title: UK: US regulators may ease Lloyd's trust fund rules.
newsitem.headline: US regulators may ease Lloyd's trust fund rules.

text.p: U.S. regulators said on Wednesday they were willing to discuss with Lloyds of London relaxing the rules on trust funds maintained by the insurance market in the U.S.

"There could be improvements in the trust fund situaton for Lloyd's, but it will take some time," Edward Muhl, superintendent of New York Insurance Department until last year, told an insurance conference.

Since 1995, Lloyd's has had to match its U.S. liabilities dollar for dollar in its trust funds. Other foreign insurers also have to keep funds in the U.S. if they do business there, but the requirements are less stringent.

Under new regulations, foreign insurance companies need to put the equivalent of 30 percent of their gross U.S. liabilities into a trust fund, with a minimum balance of $5.4 million and a maximum of $60 million.
James Brown of the Louisiana Insurance Department said the situation regarding Lloyd's had changed considerably over the last year with the implementation of the market's rescue plan.
Brown, who is insurance commissioner for the State, said that he expected discussions to take place between Lloyd's and U.S. regulators on this issue.
A spokesman for Lloyd's said the market was in constant communication with U.S. insurance regulators.
